cases.why: the title match loosens to a prefix. 'Booth audit failed: PR #10' would then land as a comment on PR #100's issue, and PR #10's failure would never get an issue of its own.
the search includes closed issues. Closing an issue is how a person says 'handled', so every later failure would be filed as a comment on a closed issue nobody is watching.
an open issue with the same title is ignored. A canary failing every night for a week would open seven issues, which is how alert fatigue starts.
a failed gh call is treated as success. The alert step would go green having raised nothing, which is the silent failure this module exists to end, one level up.
close_open_issue comments but never closes, so an alert whose cause has ended stays open for a person to find
closing with no open issue creates one, so a merged pull request with no alert raises a fresh alert about itself
cases.replace:
if number is None:
        _gh(['issue', 'create', '--title', title, '--body-file', '-'], run, stdin=comment)
        return None
    _gh(['issue', 'comment', str(number), '--body-file', '-'], run, stdin=comment)

cases.why: --log is accepted and dropped, so the alert carries only a link and the cause needs a sign-in to read (#529)
a run that died before writing its log raises an alert that says nothing about it, which hides where it stopped
cases.find: return f'{body}\n\nNo log was written ({path.name}): the run stopped before its main step.'
